title: Replacement Property Identification
name: Replacement Property Identification
metaTitle: Replacement Property Identification in Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: Building and documenting a Fort Worth replacement property candidate list, compared on a consistent framework before the 45-day deadline closes.

sections.html: Identification is a documentation exercise as much as an investment decision, and a Fort Worth investor's 45-day window is spent more efficiently when the candidate list is built and compared on a consistent framework from the start, rather than assembled from whichever listings a broker happened to send.

sections.heading: Building a Candidate List Across Asset Classes
sections.html:
We start candidate sourcing before the relinquished property closes whenever the timeline allows, pulling from industrial listings near the Alliance corridor, multifamily and net lease inventory closer to the Cultural District and Sundance Square, and medical office space near the hospital-anchored submarkets, depending on what the investor's exchange proceeds and debt capacity can support. Asset class is not fixed at the outset; a candidate list that spans two or three property types gives the investor real options if the strongest single-asset-class candidate falls through diligence.

We also weigh how much active management each asset class demands against the investor's own time and staffing, since a multifamily property with unit turnover and maintenance calls is a different day-to-day commitment than a single-tenant net lease building, and a candidate list should reflect the investor's actual capacity rather than only the highest projected return.

sections.heading: Comparing Candidates on a Consistent Framework
sections.html:
Every candidate gets evaluated against the same checklist regardless of asset class: tenant credit or occupancy stability, lease or rent roll integrity, financing feasibility inside the 180-day period, and any title or zoning issue that could delay closing. Comparing candidates on inconsistent criteria, where one property is judged mainly on cap rate and another mainly on location, makes the eventual identification decision harder to defend if a deal later falls apart.

We document why each candidate did or did not advance to the identification list, since a clear record of the comparison supports both the investor's own decision-making and the file the qualified intermediary and tax advisor will eventually reference if a question arises about the exchange's structure.

sections.heading: Documentation Standard Before a Property Is Identified
sections.html:
Before any candidate is placed on the written identification list, we confirm a defined set of records exists or is in process.

  • signed purchase contract or executed letter of intent with the seller
  • lender term sheet or preliminary approval covering the anticipated loan amount
  • title commitment ordered and reviewed for exceptions
  • lease or rent roll reconciled against underlying tenant documentation
  • qualified intermediary notified and prepared to receive the written identification

sections.heading: Backup Candidates and List Flexibility
sections.html: The three-property rule allows up to three identified candidates regardless of value, and we generally recommend using more than one slot even when an investor has a clear preference, since a title defect, a financing denial, or a seller who backs out can eliminate the lead candidate with no time left to source a replacement. A backup candidate identified in writing on day thirty is still usable; one identified after day forty-five is not.

sections.heading: Finalizing the List Before the 45-Day Deadline
sections.html: The written identification notice must reach the qualified intermediary before midnight on the 45th day, described with the specificity the regulations require, typically a street address or legal description rather than a general area or listing reference. We finalize the notice language and confirm delivery several days ahead of the deadline rather than treating the final day as a buffer for last-minute changes.

faqs.q: Why build a candidate list across more than one asset class?
faqs.a: A list spanning two or three property types gives an investor real options if the strongest single-asset-class candidate falls through diligence, financing, or title review, rather than leaving the exchange dependent on one deal closing.

faqs.q: What framework is used to compare Fort Worth replacement candidates?
faqs.a: Every candidate is evaluated against the same criteria, including tenant credit or occupancy stability, lease or rent roll integrity, financing feasibility inside the 180-day period, and any title or zoning issue that could delay closing.

faqs.q: Should an investor use all three slots under the three-property rule?
faqs.a: Using more than one slot is generally recommended even with a clear preference, since a title defect, financing denial, or seller withdrawal can eliminate the lead candidate with no time left to identify a replacement after day forty-five.

faqs.q: How specific does the written identification need to be?
faqs.a: The regulations require enough specificity to identify the exact property, typically a street address or legal description, rather than a general area or a listing reference the qualified intermediary cannot act on.

faqs.q: What documentation should exist before a property is added to the identification list?
faqs.a: A signed contract or letter of intent, a lender term sheet, an ordered title commitment, and reconciled lease or rent roll documentation should all be in process, so the identified property is realistic to close inside the 180-day period.

faqs.q: Should the highest-return candidate always be prioritized on the identification list?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The management burden of an asset class, such as unit turnover and maintenance calls on a multifamily property versus a single-tenant net lease building, should be weighed against the investor's own time and staffing capacity, rather than the projected return alone.

faqs.q: Can an identified property be swapped for a different one after the 45-day deadline passes?
faqs.a: No, once the 45th day passes the identification list is locked, so any candidate not already named in writing on that list before the deadline cannot be substituted in, regardless of how the original candidates perform in diligence afterward.
